newsitem.title: USA: U.S. SRW wheat reported in good shape in week.
newsitem.headline: U.S. SRW wheat reported in good shape in week.

text.p: Soft red winter wheat conditions mostly improved in leading producer states in the week ended May 18, according to weekly crop reports from state agricultural statistics services.

OHIO - Winter wheat ratings rose slightly amid cooler than normal temperatures and heavy rains in the northern part of the state. Wheat condition was rated 51 percent good to excellent, up one point from last week, and 12 percent poor to very poor, down 3 points. A year ago at this time, the crop was rated 25 percent good to excellent, 37 poor to very poor.
Wheat was 90 percent jointed, up 17 points on last year, but only 1 percent headed vs 8 last year, 7 on a 5-year average.
The rainfall accumulations in northern Ohio were mostly below normal as the storms passed quickly over the states.
Topsoil moisture levels were 15 percent surplus, 79 percent adequate and six percent short.

ILLINOIS - Winter wheat was 37 percent headed, versus 14 last year and 40 percent for the five-year average. Wheat condition was rated 74 percent good to excellent and 5 percent poor to very poor, both unchanged from a week earlier.
Varying amounts of frost were reported in Illinois on Friday, May 16, but crop damage was believed minimal with alfalfa the most affected, the weekly state report said.
Illinois topsoil moisture was rated one percent very short, 22 short, 72 adequate and 5 surplus.

INDIANA - Winter wheat was rated 69 percent good to excellent vs 62 a week earlier, and 4 percent rated poor to very poor versus 7 a week earlier. Wheat was 97 percent jointed vs 89 average. Wheat was 30 percent headed 10 a week ago, 21 a year ago and 27 on average.
Topsoil moisture was rated nil very short, three percent short, 60 adequate and 37 surplus.

MISSOURI - Winter wheat conditions were mostly unchanged with 11 percent rated excellent, 49 good, 29 fair, 10 poor and one very poor. About 50 percent of the wheat was headed versus 40 a year ago and the 48 average.
Topsoil moisture was rated 5 percent surplus, 66 adequate, 26 short and three very short.
